shorts.title: Ramaswamy: "It is an ad from our campaign" #Shorts
shorts.hook: Ramaswamy owns the ad about Acton's mother
shorts.narration: [serious] Ohio's governor race just got ugly. Vivek Ramaswamy's campaign put out an ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother calling her daughter a liar. Ramaswamy confirmed it on camera: [deadpan] "It is an ad from our campaign." Acton's campaign says it cost four million dollars. Ramaswamy says he has never met Acton, and that her mother was not paid. Vice President Vance said whether the ad was appropriate was not really his concern. [serious] George Washington warned about "the alternate domination of one faction over another, sharpened by the spirit of revenge." He never imagined it would be posted on social media. [beat] Four million dollars, zero meetings, and a family feud as the closing argument. That's not a campaign strategy. That's a confession that the arguments ran out. Republicans, is this really what you want your party to be remembered for? Subscribe for the daily news.

claims.text: Vivek Ramaswamy said of the ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother: "It is an ad from our campaign."
Acton's campaign says Ramaswamy invested $4 million in the ad; Ramaswamy said he has never met Acton or her mother and that the mother was not paid.
Vice President JD Vance said whether the ad was appropriate was 'not really my concern'.

shorts.title: Tiffany: "Joe Biden won" — and he'll certify 2028? #Shorts
shorts.hook: Tom Tiffany now says: "Joe Biden won"
shorts.narration: [amused] Wisconsin Republican Tom Tiffany, running for governor, now promises to certify the 2028 election. Lovely. In 2020, he voted to object to certifying results in Arizona and Pennsylvania, and backed that Texas lawsuit the Supreme Court threw out. Now his campaign says, quote, "Joe Biden won," and, "In 2028, I'll certify whoever wins the most votes in Wisconsin." [beat] Six years late, but early is the new on time. [serious] George Washington wrote that the basis of our political systems is "the right of the people to make and to alter their constitutions of government." The people, friends. Not a congressman with a pen. [beat] And the governor's signature on certification is a duty, not a vibe check. So Republicans, if Joe Biden won, what exactly was the objection for? Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: Tom Tiffany voted in 2020 to object to certification of results in Arizona and Pennsylvania and backed a Texas-led lawsuit the Supreme Court dismissed.
Tiffany's campaign statement: "Joe Biden won," and "In 2028, I'll certify whoever wins the most votes in Wisconsin."
A Marquette law professor says the governor's role in signing the certificate is more of a duty than discretion.
Washington: "The basis of our political systems is the right of the people to make and to alter their constitutions of government."

shorts.title: DOJ sues California over a thumb drive "on a sticky note" #Shorts
shorts.hook: DOJ's noncitizen list and a sticky note
shorts.narration: [incredulous] The Trump Justice Department sued California over a thumb drive. It lists about twenty thousand people the feds call likely noncitizens, and the DOJ wants a judge to stop California from counting their mail ballots. California's Secretary of State's office says the drive's password was written, quote, "on a sticky note." [beat] National security, courtesy of Post-it. California Attorney General Rob Bonta calls the move "unprecedented, baseless, lawless territory," and says a federal law bars voter roll changes within ninety days of an election. Those are his claims. And in Nevada, the feds alleged nearly sixteen thousand possible noncitizens on the rolls, and the state found all of them were citizens. [serious] The Constitution says the president "shall take Care that the Laws be faithfully executed." [beat] Faithfully. Not sticky-ly. MAGA friends, if the list is that solid, why not show your math? Subscribe!

claims.text: The DOJ sued California on Oct. 15, 2026, asking a judge to bar it from counting mail ballots of people flagged as likely noncitizens; the list of about 20,000 names was on a password-protected thumb drive.
California's Secretary of State's office said the password was written 'on a sticky note'.
Bonta said the federal move is "unprecedented, baseless, lawless territory" and that federal law bars changing voter rolls within 90 days of an election.
In Nevada, the federal government alleged nearly 16,000 possible noncitizens; the state found all were citizens.
Constitution, Art. II: the President "shall take Care that the Laws be faithfully executed".

shorts.title: Trump on Iran: "one way or the other" — after Nov. 3? #Shorts
shorts.hook: Iran war, reportedly on hold till after Nov. 3
shorts.narration: [serious] A question about timing. The Financial Times reports that Israel's Netanyahu ordered a major offensive against Iran planned for mid-October, but that Trump opposed renewed large-scale fighting before the midterms. The White House told the paper the United States would not attack before then. Trump himself says an outcome with Iran will come "one way or the other." Remember, America has been at war with Iran since February twenty-eighth, and voters get their say on November third. [serious] The Declaration of Independence says governments derive "their just powers from the consent of the governed." [beat] Consent, apparently, is easier to collect before the explosions. Now, that is the reported timeline, not mine. But, friends: should the schedule of a war ever depend on the schedule of an election? Subscribe for the daily news.

Trump said talks with Iran continue and an outcome will come 'one way or the other'.
The Iran war began February 28, 2026.

shorts.title: Ken Paxton is now tied in Texas — Fox News poll #Shorts
shorts.narration: [amused] Ken Paxton, the Trump-backed Texan who beat Senator John Cornyn in the primary, just got a Fox News poll that should make Texas Republicans sweat. Paxton and Democrat James Talarico are tied among likely voters, forty-nine to forty-nine. In September, Talarico was ahead. [beat] That's not a lead, that's a cliffhanger. In the same poll, half of those polled say Paxton is too close to Trump, and more than half of likely voters view him unfavorably. Madison wrote in Federalist 51, "If men were angels, no government would be necessary." [beat] Texas Republicans looked at their options and picked a guy who isn't one. Trump's own job rating in Texas is underwater in this poll. So MAGA friends: if you can't win Texas easily, what does that say about November? Subscribe — Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: A Fox News poll (Oct. 15-19) has Ken Paxton and James Talarico tied at 49% among likely voters; in September Talarico led 51%-49%.
Paxton defeated John Cornyn in the GOP primary and is Trump-backed.
In the poll, 50% say Paxton is too close to Trump, and his favorability is 41% favorable, 58% unfavorable.
Trump's Texas job rating in the poll is 45% approve, 54% disapprove.
Federalist 51: "If men were angels, no government would be necessary."
